knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Expectations are set before the work starts and are confirmed after the test patch, in writing.
A written record of pre-existing damage protects both the client and the business.
The test patch shows what is achievable. The discussion is recorded and the client is informed before any promise is made.
Exclusions for engineered stone and structural work are written into the scope so that the client understands the limits.
Complaints go through the business escalation route in the policy, with the records checked first.

practicalCriteria: Photographs and records pre-existing damage before work starts
Explains the expected result before the test patch and records the client's acknowledgement
States the written limits and exclusions
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Client acknowledgement of expectations and limits
stopWorkCriteria: Work the client has not agreed to in writing
Stop and report if the surface cannot be identified
